stem: What is the primary role of an audio description track in a multimedia video?

options.text: To describe essential visual actions, expressions, and scene changes during pauses in dialogue.
options.shortLabel: Describes visual actions during dialogue pauses
options.rationale: Audio description inserts spoken narration of visual content into existing pauses in the primary audio track.

options.text: To synchronize written subtitles and captions with spoken dialogue and other relevant sounds throughout the video.
options.rationale: Caption synchronization ensures that text corresponds to the timing of dialogue and meaningful audio events. This supports deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers but does not communicate visual information.

options.text: To provide a spoken reference track that can assist in generating searchable transcripts and identifying dialogue segments.
options.rationale: Spoken reference tracks and dialogue recordings can support transcription workflows and media indexing. However, generating or improving transcripts does not fulfill the purpose of describing visual information.

options.text: To separate dialogue from background music and environmental sounds, allowing viewers to adjust the relative volume of each audio component.
options.rationale: Separating dialogue, music, and sound effects can improve audio control and listening clarity. This is an audio mixing and accessibility feature rather than a method of communicating visual information.

explanation: Audio description (also referred to as described video) provides spoken narration of important visual details—such as actions, settings, facial expressions, and on-screen text—during pauses in spoken dialogue. This ensures individuals who are blind or have low vision receive equal narrative context.
author: Oxypteros
